evidence.note: Opening plan is a single undifferentiated push: 'create evaluate.py implementing all task types, run structural checks' — no per-type milestone list or done-conditions articulated up front.

Agent decides to validate type-by-type and orders by cost/risk: 'Start with smaller types (STS, summarization, pair classification) to catch coding issues before expensive retrieval/clustering/classification.' This is genuine per-type decomposition with rough ordering.

Sequentially runs run_eval per type (classification, then clustering, then retrieval), validating each before proceeding — a per-type milestone cadence, but each done-check is only structural pass, never tied to leaderboard/spec numeric agreement.
Coverage of all 37 tasks handled reactively via a merge of per-type result files rather than as pre-planned sub-goals; no explicit milestone for the CLI contract or skip-and-continue behavior.

reasoning: The agent clearly split work by the six task types and validated each type before moving on, with a rough cost/risk-based ordering (cheap types first to surface coding bugs), which squarely matches the level-5 anchor. It falls short of level 8 because the per-milestone done-checks were purely structural (run_eval passes), never gated on leaderboard/spec numeric agreement, and there were no distinct milestones for the CLI contract or skip-and-continue behavior; 37-dataset coverage was handled reactively via merging rather than tracked as explicit sub-goals.
